name: FJPW Icon Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Announced as FJPW's own top prize from the fed's own founding handbook onward, meant to be crowned by a 32-man single-elimination tournament (named, across three successive announcements, the E-1 Invitational's own "Chamber of Horrors," a "Torture Chamber" match, and finally a "Deathdome" cage) at the fed's own mid-November 1997 pay-per-view. No result for that event survives in this collection's own holdings, and no reign was ever recorded under either name the tournament was billed under.
notes: FJPW's own founding handbook (27 September 1997) and FAQ v2.5 (9 November 1997); the tournament's own successive announcements of 1, 15, 24 and 26 October 1997.

name: FJPW Asian Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Billed by the fed's own FAQ as the Icon Heavyweight Championship's own top contender's prize, nicknamed "Mr. Endurance" for its stated near-nightly defense schedule. No reign was ever recorded in this collection's own holdings.
notes: FJPW's own FAQ v2.5 (9 November 1997); not named in the earlier handbooks.

name: FJPW Juniorweight Championship
epitaph: Announced as the top prize of FJPW's own J-Crown/Juniorweight division (220 lbs and under). No reign was ever recorded in this collection's own holdings.
notes: FJPW's own founding handbook (27 September 1997) and FAQ v2.5 (9 November 1997).

name: FJPW Icon Tag Team Championships
epitaph: Announced across three successive card previews to be decided by a multi-team inverted cage battle royal -- first at the fed's own mid-November pay-per-view, then again on a separate proposed weekly card -- naming the Lion's Den among the intended entrants each time. No result for either event survives in this collection's own holdings, and no reign was ever recorded.
notes: FJPW's own founding handbook (27 September 1997), card previews of 15, 24 and 26 October 1997, and the RAGE weekly-show announcement of 10 November 1997.
